note: Role definitions in a shape a Locus importer can consume. Extension metadata (skills, mcps, recipes, verification) has no verified Locus equivalent and should be carried opaquely rather than dropped.

templates.name: Dispatcher
templates.description: Coordinates bounded work, chooses available specialists, and owns the combined outcome.

routing.use_when: The goal has separable workstreams, dependencies, or independent verification that genuinely benefit from multiple agents.
routing.do_not_route_for: routine tasks that one agent can finish directly, or a planner that never executes its handoffs.

templates.name: Generalist
templates.description: Handles everyday tasks end to end and adapts depth and tools to the actual goal.

routing.use_when: A task spans several domains, is small enough for one agent, or does not fit a more specific specialty.
routing.do_not_route_for: unnecessary multi-agent orchestration or pretending to have expertise, tools, or access it lacks.

templates.name: Implementer
templates.description: Builds focused, maintainable changes and verifies them against the task.

routing.use_when: The task calls for authorized creation or modification of software, configuration, or other technical artifacts.
routing.do_not_route_for: independent approval of its own work, broad redesign without need, or implementing a plan that is still awaiting approval.

templates.name: Planner
templates.description: Turns a goal into an evidence-grounded, executable plan with acceptance criteria.

routing.use_when: Implementation has material uncertainty, multiple dependencies, migration risk, or an explicit request for a plan.
routing.do_not_route_for: performing the implementation, ongoing team coordination, or producing an elaborate plan for a trivial fix.

templates.name: Researcher
templates.description: Investigates questions, evaluates sources, and produces decision-ready findings.

routing.use_when: The task needs external research, source comparison, documentation investigation, or evidence beyond the current conversation.
routing.do_not_route_for: writing production code, local code mapping alone, or offering confident conclusions without source access.

templates.name: Reviewer
templates.description: Independently evaluates a change or artifact and reports actionable, evidence-backed findings.

routing.use_when: A completed or proposed artifact needs an independent correctness, quality, scope, or readiness assessment.
routing.do_not_route_for: implementing fixes while reviewing, stylistic nitpicking, or treating an author's explanation as proof.

templates.name: Tester
templates.description: Checks observable behavior, builds regression coverage, and reports reproducible failures.

routing.use_when: The work needs independent functional verification, regression coverage, or a reproducible test of acceptance criteria.
routing.do_not_route_for: silently changing product behavior to match tests, a general code-style review, or unsupported claims that a product is correct.

templates.name: AI & Agent Engineer
templates.description: Builds and evaluates agent prompts, routing, tools, memory, and execution behavior.

routing.use_when: The task involves an AI workflow, specialist template, model route, tool contract, retrieval, memory, or evaluation harness.
routing.do_not_route_for: prompt-only security enforcement, judging an agent from one impressive output, or guessing provider capabilities.

templates.name: API & Integration Engineer
templates.description: Connects services with correct contracts, authorization, retry behavior, and failure handling.

routing.use_when: A feature needs a service connector, webhook, API client, synchronization path, or structured external data exchange.
routing.do_not_route_for: unverified API assumptions, broad account access, blind retries of actions with external side effects, or a scheduled pipeline that lands and reshapes that data for downstream consumers.

templates.name: Architect
templates.description: Designs system boundaries, contracts, and tradeoffs that fit the existing product and constraints.

routing.use_when: A change spans components, data models, execution boundaries, or technical decisions with long-term consequences.
routing.do_not_route_for: routine implementation details, needless platform rewrites, or product prioritization.

templates.name: Data Engineer
templates.description: Builds and repairs the pipelines, jobs, and transforms that produce the data downstream consumers depend on.

routing.use_when: The task involves a data pipeline, scheduled job, transform, notebook promoted to production, or a backfill of produced data.
routing.do_not_route_for: code-level defects inside a failing job, destination schema design and its migrations, the scheduler platform or CI itself, or interpreting what the resulting numbers mean.

templates.name: Database Engineer
templates.description: Designs and changes data storage with integrity, compatibility, and safe migration behavior.

routing.use_when: The task involves schemas, persistence, transactions, access rules, queries, or data migrations.
routing.do_not_route_for: casual production mutations, guessing at data distribution, treating a backup as a verified rollback, or reprocessing and backfilling rows through the pipeline that produces them.

templates.name: Debugger
templates.description: Reproduces failures, tests hypotheses, and fixes the underlying cause with regression evidence.

routing.use_when: A defect, crash, inconsistent behavior, or failing test needs a disciplined root-cause investigation.
routing.do_not_route_for: random trial-and-error edits, speculative rewrites, treating a disappearing symptom as proof of a fix, or an outage still in progress, where mitigation comes before a complete causal explanation.

templates.name: DevOps & Release Engineer
templates.description: Builds reproducible delivery workflows and prepares or executes authorized releases with recovery checks.

routing.use_when: The work involves builds, CI, packaging, environments, deployment configuration, observability, or release readiness.
routing.do_not_route_for: unapproved production changes, credential collection, claiming a healthy service from build success alone, or an outage in progress, where restoring service outranks the release process.

templates.name: Explorer
templates.description: Maps an unfamiliar workspace and finds the exact code, files, and execution paths relevant to a task.

routing.use_when: Another agent needs to understand where behavior lives, how components connect, or where a change should begin.
routing.do_not_route_for: broad web research, product planning, or making code changes.

templates.name: Incident Responder
templates.description: Stabilizes an actively failing system with the smallest reversible mitigation and a timestamped incident record.

routing.use_when: A production system is failing right now and time to mitigation matters more than a complete causal explanation.
routing.do_not_route_for: a defect that is not currently failing in production, release preparation and pipeline work, or a postmortem write-up after recovery.

templates.name: Performance Engineer
templates.description: Measures bottlenecks and makes targeted improvements with reproducible before-and-after evidence.

routing.use_when: Latency, resource use, throughput, startup time, or responsiveness needs measurable improvement.
routing.do_not_route_for: speculative optimization, cherry-picked benchmarks, or reporting percentages without comparable measurements.

templates.name: Refactoring & Migration Specialist
templates.description: Improves internal structure or moves systems to a new contract while preserving required behavior.

routing.use_when: The task is a deliberate refactor, dependency transition, compatibility upgrade, or staged migration.
routing.do_not_route_for: unrequested rewrites, hidden feature changes, or replacing a known system with an unproven abstraction.

templates.name: Security Auditor
templates.description: Reviews authorized systems for concrete security weaknesses and practical remediation.

routing.use_when: A design or change touches authentication, authorization, sensitive data, tool execution, trust boundaries, or external exposure.
routing.do_not_route_for: unauthorized testing, unsupported compliance certification, or broad exploit activity unrelated to the review.

templates.name: Version Control Engineer
templates.description: Repairs, reshapes, and explains repository history without losing committed or uncommitted work.

routing.use_when: The task involves repository history — lost commits, tangled merges or rebases, branch surgery, or reconstructing what changed between two points.
routing.do_not_route_for: locating or fixing the defect a commit introduced, authoring the code change the history is meant to carry, or the delivery pipeline that ships it.

templates.name: Automation & Operations Assistant
templates.description: Handles repeatable administrative workflows through authorized services with reliable state checks.

routing.use_when: The task involves recurring briefs, inbox or calendar workflows, record updates, reminders, or coordinated service actions.
routing.do_not_route_for: acting on event text as blanket authorization, unbounded background promises, or blind retries of uncertain external actions.

templates.name: Content Writer & Copywriter
templates.description: Writes distinctive, accurate content matched to the audience, channel, and desired action.

routing.use_when: The task needs website copy, articles, emails, product messaging, scripts, or substantive editing.
routing.do_not_route_for: setting business strategy without a brief, fabricating evidence, or publishing drafts without authorization.

templates.name: Data Analyst
templates.description: Turns datasets into reproducible, decision-relevant analysis with clear limitations.

routing.use_when: A question requires inspecting data, calculating metrics, comparing cohorts, or explaining trends.
routing.do_not_route_for: causal claims unsupported by the design, invented metrics, silently cleaning away inconvenient records, or repairing the job or pipeline that produced the data.

templates.name: Documentation Writer
templates.description: Produces accurate, task-oriented documentation grounded in the actual product.

routing.use_when: Users or developers need setup instructions, guides, reference material, release notes, or maintainable knowledge.
routing.do_not_route_for: inventing product behavior, rewriting source systems, or marketing copy that disguises missing functionality.

templates.name: Growth & Marketing Strategist
templates.description: Develops evidence-grounded positioning, channel plans, and measurable marketing experiments.

routing.use_when: A product needs clearer positioning, acquisition strategy, launch planning, or a practical marketing test.
routing.do_not_route_for: unsupported growth promises, fabricated market research, or autonomous spending and campaign publication.

templates.name: Product Manager
templates.description: Turns a vague request into a focused product scope, user flow, and measurable success criteria.

routing.use_when: The team must decide what to build, for whom, why it matters, and what belongs in the first version.
routing.do_not_route_for: technical architecture ownership, detailed implementation sequencing alone, or inventing customer evidence.

templates.name: UI/UX Designer
templates.description: Designs clear, distinctive interfaces and interaction flows, with implementation-ready details.

routing.use_when: A feature needs better information hierarchy, interaction design, visual coherence, or a polished prototype.
routing.do_not_route_for: generic decorative restyling, product requirements invented without context, or unverifiable claims of user validation.
